newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares post losses, pivotals take lead.
newsitem.headline: India shares post losses, pivotals take lead.

text.p: Indian stocks retreated on Thursday as profit-taking snapped a two-day winning streak, dealers said.
"We have been expecting a correction, but it remains to be seen if this is a temporary reaction," Manish Gupta, research analyst at Khandwala Securities, a local brokerage firm said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) dropped 90.92 points or 2.72 percent to 3,250.94.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index fell 18.52 points or 1.94 percent to 932.77 and the CRISIL 500-share index lost 12.09 points or 1.90 percent to 624.56.
"The market was overheated. It's more of a sentiment-driven rally with the big guys (foreign institutional investors) not operating in a big way," Gupta told Reuters.
Dealers said the market reaction was expected after the Bombay share index rallied about 212 points or 6.7 percent in two straight days.
Pivotals like bank major State Bank of India and steel giant Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO) which led the market rally bore the selling brunt on Thursday.
Shares of TISCO fell 6.75 rupees to 186.0 while SBI lost 14.20 rupees to 225.75.
ACC lost 80.70 rupees to 1,565.0, Reliance 5.75 to 209.0, SBI 14.20 to 225.75, TISCO 6.75 to 186.0, TELCO 17.70 to 424.50 and ITC 11.0 to 311.50.
The Delhi exchange index dropped 18.05 points to 733.70 and the Calcutta index 5.72 points to 430.93.
